readerPresentationReview.scope: First-read chapter threads, key-term navigation, progressive disclosure and clearly labelled hypothetical worked examples. This revision adds 13 distinct worked examples or explanatory sections to the 13 chapters previously below the non-gating 850-word soft target. All additions use existing governed module claims and sources; no claim IDs, source records, reader prompts or acceptance requirements were added.

addedSectionTitlesByModule.material-families: Quick guide to common material properties

latestRevision.rationale: Added a collapsible, source-linked quick guide to the existing material-families module. It distinguishes flow, mechanical, thermal, shrinkage, density and moisture test results; each row names the applicable method and what the result cannot establish. Ten new ISO source records were added, with no new claim IDs, process settings or production authority. The guide remains within the module's technical-review status.

addedSectionTitlesByModule.hot-runners: Worked example (hypothetical): a colour mark after a production interruption
addedSectionTitlesByModule.ejection-draft: Worked example (hypothetical): a part distorts while leaving one core
addedSectionTitlesByModule.documentation: Worked example (hypothetical): hand over a baseline another shift can interpret
addedSectionTitlesByModule.process-window: Worked example (hypothetical): build a process window from a sequence of questions
addedSectionTitlesByModule.diagnostic-method: Worked example (hypothetical): a short shot appears after an interruption
addedSectionTitlesByModule.warpage: Worked example (hypothetical): a reinforced panel bows after release
addedSectionTitlesByModule.black-specks: Worked example (hypothetical): compare an all-cavity event with a one-cavity event
addedSectionTitlesByModule.weld-lines: Worked example (hypothetical): assess a line downstream of a hole
addedSectionTitlesByModule.cavity-pressure: Worked example (hypothetical): interpret a changed trace before changing an alarm

revisionHistory.conclusion: Added 13 distinct explanatory or hypothetical example sections to the 13 chapters that were below the 850-word non-gating soft target. Each is tied to an existing module claim scope; no claim IDs, evidence sources, reader prompts or acceptance requirements were added. All 21 first-read chapters now meet or exceed the soft target. Independent human SME review and device validation remain HOLD.
revisionHistory.rationale: The compact chapters needed concrete applications of their existing mechanisms and evidence rules. The examples show how to preserve cavity, time, measurement and material context, compare predictions, and state uncertainty. They add learning depth without prescribing universal settings or repeating summary sections.

revisionHistory.conclusion: Expanded r03 with five beginner-friendly polymer-science sections on repeat units, molecular-weight distributions, branching and entanglement, thermal transitions, cooling-rate evidence and polymer measurement methods. Expanded r03a with six advanced sections on spatial fibre-orientation fields, micro-CT/model comparison, directional measurement planning, grade/system compatibility, thermal history and supplier-document interpretation. Added three primary/standards evidence records to existing claim scopes; no claim IDs or process recipes were added.
revisionHistory.rationale: The beginner path now explains chain populations and molecular architecture, distinguishes glass transition, melting and crystallisation, and teaches what DSC and other measurements can establish. The advanced follow-up is more than twice its prior first-read length and develops evidence planning for both fibre-reinforced parts and demanding material changes. The LDPE, polypropylene and DSC examples are limited to the sources, samples and methods described; they do not establish generic machine settings or product acceptance.
revisionHistory.materialChapterEmphasis: r03 now builds from repeat units through molecular-weight distribution, branching, entanglement, thermal transitions, crystallisation and measurement limits before returning to grade identity and part evidence. r03a follows with deeper spatial orientation and material-system review. r18 and r19 retain their existing dimensional-stability and thin-wall/multi-cavity focus.

what-injection-moulding-is: How to think like a process engineer
Think in linked stages, not isolated settings
Inputs, process signals and outputs are different kinds of evidence
Follow the process as a chain of handoffs
cycle: Treat the cycle as an interacting system
Each stage hands conditions to the next
The stages interact across the cycle
machine-anatomy: Read the machine as interacting subsystems
Read commanded and actual values as different evidence
mould-anatomy: Follow the complete path through the mould
Use location to connect a symptom to mould features
safety-foundations: A stopped screen is not an isolation
Stored energy persists when motion stops
Choose evidence collection that stays within the safe boundary
Safety controls define the boundary of process work
polymer-structure: Do not turn the categories into absolutes
Structure influences the way a moulding responds to heat and flow
Amorphous and semi-crystalline are useful categories, not complete recipes
Morphology can vary within one part
Cooling gives the material a local structural history
Think of a polymer as chains with different freedom to move
Glass transition and melting are different landmarks
rheology: Flow resistance is not a single material number
Pressure is evidence about the whole flow path
Compare pressure only when the flow conditions are understood
moisture-drying: Moisture state is a condition to verify
Dryer performance and material exposure are separate questions
thermal-history: Look for evidence of changing residence or degradation
Treat temperature and residence as a path through the equipment
material-families: Family names describe tendencies, not production windows
Use family knowledge to ask better questions
Compare materials by the behaviour relevant to the decision
Connect family behaviour to observable process evidence
Read a supplier property as bounded evidence
Recognize family names without treating them as complete identities
fillers-additives: Modifiers change more than one property at a time
Treat formulation changes as process changes
Relate modifier effects to direction and position
plasticising-unit: The non-return valve matters during injection
Recovery repeatability is a useful process signal
Recovery meters a shot while preparing the next melt quantity
shot-utilisation: Use cushion and screw position as trends, not verdicts
Evaluate machine fit as a group of constraints
velocity-pressure: Velocity command and pressure demand are different quantities
A process should distinguish control from limits
Compare commanded velocity with achieved motion
vp-transfer: Confirm transfer robustness, not only one ideal cycle
clamp: Why a single formula is not enough
Projected area is a model input, not the whole decision
cooling: Cooling is a heat-flow problem, not only a timer
Measure multiple links in the cooling chain
ejection-draft: Do not cure tooling problems blindly
process-baseline: Record what can reproduce the state
A baseline records state, not just setpoints
documentation: Link each engineering change to a question
Preserve material, cavity and timing context
diagnostic-method: Write competing mechanisms and predicted evidence
Verify recovery and guard against coincidence
short-shot: Use cavity comparison in multi-cavity moulds
flash: Map flash before changing clamp or pressure
Separate mould condition from process pressure history
sink-voids: Surface sink and internal void are different outcomes
Internal evidence can contradict surface appearance
splay: Appearance is not a unique diagnosis
weld-lines: Quality depends on the meeting conditions
Treat location as a design-process interaction
Geometry can dominate where the line forms
Appearance and structural consequence are not identical
Location is often a design-process interaction
black-specks: Separate continuous contamination from event-driven contamination
cavity-pressure: Use the trace as evidence of sequence
Read the trace as a sequence
doe: Replication and confirmation protect against chance findings
high-performance-polymers: The label does not define a process
Material change can change equipment compatibility
complex-diagnostics: Rank hypotheses by consequence as well as likelihood

revisionHistory.conclusion: Removed 135 repeated or summary sections across 35 governed modules, including the 53 sections previously hidden from the first read. The runtime now presents every remaining authored section directly. The retained material stays within the existing governed claims and evidence; no claims, sources, prompts or examples were added or changed.
revisionHistory.rationale: Same-module introductions and summaries often restated fuller sections later in the same module. Removing those repeats shortens the reading path while preserving distinct mechanisms, evidence checks, examples and safety guidance. Cross-chapter reminders remain where each chapter needs its own context.
